name: Gonzalo de Berceo
bio: Gonzalo de Berceo (c. 1190 - c. 1264) is the first Castilian poet known by name. A secular priest educated at the Benedictine monastery of San Millán de la Cogolla in La Rioja, he wrote devotional verse in the learned style of the mester de clerecía, chiefly in the monorhymed four-line stanza called the cuaderna vía.

His surviving works are saints' lives, poems on the Mass and the Virgin, and above all the Milagros de Nuestra Señora, twenty-five miracles of the Virgin Mary that he tells in a plain, homely Riojan Castilian for a lay audience. The text here follows the 1780 edition of Tomás Antonio Sánchez.
